decisionBox.changed: Position flips from REDUCE to ADD, but the size is deliberately small and it is spot only. The endday REDUCE was a leverage decision and it has now been executed by the market rather than by a discretionary choice: the 79,620.0 resting stop on the 27 USDT futures long sat 50.0 points above the 79,570.0 low and was taken out. What replaces it is not a new directional bet - it is a routine core add after a one-sided long flush, with no leverage and cash held back.

liquidation.note: 1,191,230 USD across 66 fills, 1,151,303 of it SHORT against only 39,927 long. This is the same cluster the endday report flagged and the read has not changed: it is a SPENT magnet. The shorts stacked there were forced to buy during the overnight push to 80,113.3 and have already bought. With price now 189.3 points beneath it, what is left overhead is a ceiling made of people who no longer have a position, not a pull.

869,402 USD across 30 fills and 100 percent LONG with zero short liquidations - a bucket that did not exist at the endday read and was still only 52,835 USD ninety minutes ago. This is the freshest and most informative thing on the map: the leverage that had been quietly building on the long side since Friday was flushed in a single move down to 79,570.0, and price recovered 240.7 points off it inside fifteen minutes. Flagged magnet because it is the nearest cluster below and because a level that has just eaten that much long size usually gets retested.

7,970 USD across 4 fills, 100 percent short and essentially unchanged from the endday read - the same small pocket, still not doing any work. It sits 60.7 points under spot and matters only as the first thing price would slice through on the way back to 79,570.

Price remains above all four averages and the stack is in order, but the histogram is negative at -64.4 and widening from -50.9 at endday, so the frame is decelerating rather than turning.

Unambiguously bullish and untouched by anything that happened overnight. Price is 4.9 percent above the 20 EMA, 11.7 percent above the 50 and 9.9 percent above the 200, and the 4,881-point gap between spot and the daily 20 is the whole reason a 543-point overnight range does not change the higher-frame read. RSI at 66.8 is high but not extended. The negative histogram is the only caution and it has been negative for several sessions without producing a daily lower low.

calibration.rollingRecord: Settled-close gates: 20 correct out of the last 21 evaluated sessions. BOTH endday gates resolved correctly, and the reduce gate did so by the narrowest margin yet recorded. The 79,570.0 reduce level required a settled 1H close beneath it; the session low printed EXACTLY 79,570.0 to the tick in the 07:00 UTC hour and the lowest settled hourly close was 79,781.2, still 211.2 points clear. The 80,315.0 add gate did not arm - the session high was 80,113.3, 201.7 points short. That is eight consecutive sessions in which a gate placed roughly 0.5 hourly ATRs beyond a proven wick has resolved correctly. The single failure in the window remains the 03 September midday add gate placed below an untested high.
calibration.note: actingHelped for this run is null and will be evaluated by the morning session. What can already be settled is the endday DECISION, and it was correct for a reason endday did not fully anticipate. Endday halved the futures long rather than exiting it and left the 79,620.0 resting stop untouched, explicitly preferring to be taken out by a wick it could not watch. That is exactly what happened: the low reached 79,570.0, the stop filled at 79,620.0, and the remaining 27 USDT of 3x long was closed for roughly -0.14 USDT instead of riding a 869,402 USD long flush with full size. Halving cost about 0.07 USDT of avoided loss relative to holding, which is small in absolute terms and completely right in process terms. The lesson endday wrote down - size down as each leg of a thesis breaks rather than defending or abandoning it - has now paid twice in two sessions.
